His wandering step . . . Conceals.] The Poet’s first wanderings take him back through the world’s
youth (122) towards the birth of time (128). According to Diodorus Siculus (III i–vii), Ethiopia was
the most ancient civilisation, from which Memphis and Thebes (Luxor) in Egypt had been colonised;
while Volney (Ruins 19) explains that Jerusalem and Tyre (both at their greatest in Solomon’s day)
were destroyed by the kings of Nineveh and Babylon. Greek civilisation was the latest ruin of time.
 Geographically the journey is round the eastern Mediterranean and up the Nile: Tyre and Balbec
(Baalbek) were in Lebanon; Babylon was in Iraq, south of Baghdad.
